arxiv-2011-01854.title: Electroneutrality Breakdown in Nanopore Arrays
arxiv-2011-01854.creator: J. Pedro de Souza 1, Amir Levy 2, Martin Z. Bazant 1,3
arxiv-2011-01854.description: Abstract The electrostatic screening of charge in one-dimensional confinement leads to long-range breakdown in electroneutrality within a nanopore. Through a series of continuum simulations, we demonstrate the principles of electroneutrality breakdown for electrolytes in one dimensional confinement. We show how interacting pores in a membrane can counteract the phenomenon of electroneutrality breakdown, eventually returning to electroneutrality.

arxiv-2106-12305.title: Non-Hermitian chiral anomalies
arxiv-2106-12305.creator: Sharareh Sayyad, Julia D. Hannukainen, Adolfo G. Grushin
arxiv-2106-12305.description: Abstract The chiral anomaly underlies a broad number of phenomena, from enhanced electronic transport in topological metals to anomalous currents in the quark-gluon plasma. The discovery of topological states of matter in non-Hermitian systems raises the question of whether there are anomalous conservation laws that remain unaccounted for.

arxiv-2305-17310.title: DotHash: Estimating Set Similarity Metrics for Link Prediction and Document Deduplication Conference: Proceedings of the 29th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining; August 6–10, 2023; Long Beach, CA, USA Proceedings of the 29th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and
arxiv-2305-17310.creator: Igor Nunes, Mike Heddes, Pere Vergés, Danny Abraham, Alex Veidenbaum, Alex Nicolau, Tony Givargis
arxiv-2305-17310.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Igor Nunes, Mike Heddes, Pere Vergés, Danny Abraham, Alex Veidenbaum, Alex Nicolau, Tony Givargis. Metrics for set similarity are a core aspect of several data mining tasks. To remove duplicate results in a Web search, for example, a common approach looks at the Jaccard index between all pairs of pages. In social network analysis, a much-celebrated metric is the Adamic-Adar index , widely used to compare node neighborhood sets in the important problem of predicting links.

arxiv-2408-07869.title: A Systematic Evaluation of Generated Time Series and Their Effects in Self-Supervised Pretraining
arxiv-2408-07869.creator: Audrey Der † , Chin-Chia Michael Yeh*, Xin Dai*, Huiyuan Chen*, Yan Zheng*, Yujie Fan*, Zhongfang Zhuang*, Vivian Lai*, Junpeng Wang*, Liang Wang*, Wei Zhang*, Eamonn Keogh † ader003@ucr.edu, miyeh@visa.com
arxiv-2408-07869.description: Abstract . Self-supervised Pretrained Models (PTMs) have demonstrated remarkable performance in computer vision and natural language processing tasks. These successes have prompted researchers to design PTMs for time series data. In our experiments, most self-supervised time series PTMs were surpassed by simple supervised models. We hypothesize this undesired phenomenon may be caused by data scarcity.

pmc-13292057.title: Cytokine markers in intracerebral hemorrhage are linked to ventricular imaging and outcomes
pmc-13292057.creator: Gracey Sorensen, Lauren Grychowski, Jennifer Yan, Will Remillard, Alice Lidman, Tori Edwards, Alison L. Herman, Conor W. Johnson, Kevin N. Sheth, Charles Matouk, Guido J. Falcone, Emily J. Gilmore, Seyedmehdi Payabvash, Lauren H. Sansing, Jessica Magid-Bernstein
pmc-13292057.description: Objective:Central nervous system (CNS) inflammation after intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is substantial, but its relationship to radiographic severity and outcome remains unclear. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) obtained via external ventricular drains (EVDs) offers a direct window into CNS inflammation. We hypothesized that a stronger proinflammatory CSF cytokine response would be associated with ventricular enlargement and worse functional outcome.

pmc-13293245.title: Evaluating acute and post-acute COVID-19 symptoms among patients with and without alcohol-related cirrhosis: implications for quality management

pmc-13293245.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundPatient-reported symptoms following COVID-19 exposure have been understudied in cirrhosis. This study evaluated type, severity, and persistence of symptoms along with impact on quality of life (QOL) post-SARS-CoV-2 infection in a cohort with and without alcohol-related cirrhosis.MethodsPatients with cirrhosis receiving care in hepatology clinics at three institutions were surveyed for symptoms and liver disease QOL (LDQOL) using standardized instruments following SARS-CoV-2 infection.

pmc-13312793.title: Prevention of cognitive decline and dementia: Current evidence on lifestyle factors and dietary patterns
pmc-13312793.creator: Ligia J. Dominguez, Nicola Veronese, Francesco Saverio Ragusa, Flavia Seminara, Salvatore Maria Baio, Laura Vernuccio, Giuseppina Catanese, Mario Barbagallo
pmc-13312793.description: Cognitive decline and dementia represent major and growing global health challenges, driven largely by population aging and increased longevity. Currently, more than 55 million people worldwide live with dementia, a figure projected to rise to approximately 153 million by 2050. Alzheimer's disease accounts for the majority of cases, and despite extensive research, effective disease-modifying therapies remain limited.

uslaw-usc-t10-s10153.title: 10 U.S.C. § 10153 — Standby Reserve: status of members
uslaw-usc-t10-s10153.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t10-s10153.description: United States Code, Title 10 (Armed Forces); Part I (Organization And Administration); Chapter 1005 (Elements Of Reserve Components). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. While in an inactive status, a Reserve is not eligible for pay or promotion and (as provided in section 12734(a) of this title) does not accrue credit for years of service under chapter 1223 of this title.

uslaw-usc-t44-s1709.title: 44 U.S.C. § 1709 — Blank forms: printing and sale to public
uslaw-usc-t44-s1709.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t44-s1709.description: United States Code, Title 44 (Public Printing And Documents); Chapter 17 (Distribution And Sale Of Public Documents). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The Director of the Government Publishing Office may print for sale by the Superintendent of Documents to the public, upon prepayment, additional copies of approved Government blank forms.
